Definition: to bubble up or froth (as boiling water), i.e. (figuratively) to be unimportant
BiblicalUsage: Pâchaz is to bubble up, to froth, to be reckless and wanton. Abimelech hires vain and light persons with pieces of silver from the house of Baal-berith, and they follow him.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that froth has no weight: men who are light and reckless are cheap to hire and quick to follow a violent leader.
